coordinates.origin: Identity root at center of grounded four-foot footprint; tail extent does not recenter origin.

concept.reason: Real specimen-based cast and skull images sufficient.

classification: Dinosauria, Ornithischia, Thyreophora; placement finer than Thyreophora varies among analyses
scope: Whole original elongate quadruped with organized low armour rows.

scale.basis: NHM Dino Directory approximate genus size, not exact length of photographed David Sole specimen.

specimen_basis: Charmouth Heritage Coast Centre official images of restored cast based on David Sole2000 specimen and skull closeup; explicitly cast/display, not untouched fossil rock.
diagnostic_targets: Elongate deep-bodied four-legged thyreophoran, short forelimbs and stronger longer hindlimbs, not pancaked ankylosaur.
Repeated low keeled osteoderms in longitudinal/parasagittal dorsal and flank rows extending neck body tail; smaller scattered low scutes between rows.
Long tapering tail no club or terminal giant spikes.
Small wedge-shaped herbivorous head, narrow front, broader rear; modest rear-skull horn knobs consistent with pictured specimen, not giant ceratopsian horns.
Neck remains visible and four feet grounded, joint transitions coherent.
uncertainties: Armour exact count and complete life arrangement not copied as measured; simplify consistent rows based on fossil pattern.
Posterior skull projections seen in specific specimen; sexual interpretation not established and not encoded.
Fleshy contour, skin colour and modest keratin covering inferred.
Photos show cast/restoration; no claim original specimen directly inspected.
acceptance_checks: Whole elongated quadruped, four legs, neck and long tapering tail.
Low repeated keeled armour in rows clearly visible without huge plates.
No tailclub or thagomizer, no oversized shoulder horns.
handoff_contract: Same directory maker QA, maker COMPLETE fixedhash stops; root async backup local-first integration, no maker upload cleanup.

style.palette: warm olive skin, muted ochre belly and ivory-tan armour; wholly artistic
style.purpose: individually inspectable static museum asset; no historical skin-colour claim
